ashwin: Heads-up: support ticket #3421 — customer on Dedicated is seeing a sudden spike in 5xx/429 errors after our latest client generator run. They say both python and ts SDKs started behaving differently. Raising since this looks like a cross-SDK regen regression.
maria: Got the customer's logs. Pattern: a single user request triggers immediate retry storms (no backoff) -> downstream rate limiter -> lots of 429s then some 500s. They were on py-sdk v1.2.4 (published last Thursday). Repro curl I ran against our staging: 
```bash
for i in {1..5}; do curl -s -I -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}'; done
```
Logs show: 
```
POST /v1/generate 200 0.12s
POST /v1/generate 429 Retry-After: 0
py-sdk retry attempt 1 -> immediate retry
py-sdk retry attempt 2 -> immediate retry
POST /v1/generate 500
```
This is reproducible locally if I force Retry-After: 0.

logan: That matches what I saw in a quick audit. The OpenAPI spec we merged added an `x-retry-policy` extension (intended to be metadata), the generator accidentally translated that into a default retry policy with no backoff for all idempotent endpoints. The new client templates set `enableAutoRetry=true` and `backoff: none`. I filed a revert PR earlier today (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-gen/pull/812).

ashwin: Oof. Customer is also reporting a billing spike because each retry consumed tokens on our hosted endpoints. We need an emergency mitigation (rollback or patch default) and a customer credit plan. Who can cut a quick patch release toggling `enableAutoRetry=false`? Also need to check TS and Go SDKs for the same behavior.

devex-bot: CI: SDK regen job completed for master — artifacts: ts-sdk@3.0.0-next, py-sdk@1.2.4, go-sdk@0.9.8. Smoke tests: flaky (see logs: https://ci.internal/regen/812).

maria: Repro steps I gave support: minimal Python snippet that reproduces immediate retries: 
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$KEY")
res = client.generate("hello", timeout=2)
# With a mocked server returning Retry-After: 0, the SDK fires retries back-to-back
```
I can produce a gist with full logs and the script. Also confirmed TS SDK (ts-sdk@3.0.0-next) exhibits same immediate retry behaviour in node.

logan: Short-term plan: revert the generator template change (PR 812) -> publish patched releases that restore exponential backoff -> coordinate canary with a single customer's key. Medium-term: add cross-SDK integration tests in the regen pipeline that assert backoff respects Retry-After and doesn't treat 0/empty as immediate bomb. Also add a changelog lint rule so generator changes that affect defaults get explicit changelog entries.

ashwin: Good. Maria — can you prepare the repro gist + suggested rollback verification steps so support can validate once we publish patches? I'll draft a credit note for the customer's billing spike. Also tag release-engineering for fast-track.

maria: On it. I also noticed the changelog for the generator run didn't mention the retry default change — we should treat that as a release note gap. I'll add a quick checklist item to the regen CI job.

support-bot: Support ticket #3421 updated: told customer we are investigating and provisionally disabled auto-retry on their tenant. ETA: 2h for patch and verification.

logan: I'll open the hotfix branch and ping @release-engineering now. If we need to yank published packages, we may need to revoke the pyproject & npm artifacts (coordination required).

ashwin: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here. If we end up reverting packages please list exact versions to revoke and affected tenants.

maria: I'll post the gist and a short test matrix (py/ts/go + versions) once I finish reproducer. Should have it in ~30m.

logan: FYI putting a blocker on the regen pipeline until we have the regression tests in place. Can't have silent behavior changes in defaults.

ashwin: Agreed. We'll follow up after the patch.
